punchline: Thich Nhat Hanh says the main cause of anger is a seed in us that has been watered too often.
thirty_sec: Thich Nhat Hanh finds the main cause of our suffering in the seed of anger inside us. That seed has been watered too often, by other people and by ourselves. Without water a seed does not grow, but without a seed the water grows nothing. So the book advises selective watering: you choose which seeds to feed, to protect yourself and the people you love. When anger rises, you breathe mindfully and try not to say or do anything yet.
key_contrast: the seed, not the other person
